stem.text: Let \( f(x) = 8 \ln\left(1 + \frac{x - 4}{3}\right) \). The Taylor series for f about \( x = 4 \) is \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{8 (-1)^{n+1} \left(x - 4\right)^{n}}{n \cdot 3^{n}} \). Its radius of convergence is \( 3 \). Does the series converge to f at \( x = 7 \)? Give a reason for the answer.

answer_key.label: Yes, because \( x = 7 \) is an endpoint that the interval of convergence \( 1 < x \le 7 \) includes.

worked_solution.text: The ratio test gives convergence for \( \left|x - 4\right| < 3 \), the interior \( 1 < x < 7 \), and \( x = 7 \) is an endpoint.
At \( x = 7 \) the series is \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{8 (-1)^{n+1}}{n} \), which converges by the alternating series test, so the interval of convergence is \( 1 < x \le 7 \).
